text:
Maya (Design): Heads up — I prototyped an alternate for metric tiles on narrow viewports: instead of collapsing into a vertical stack, they turn into a horizontal swipeable carousel. Feels less noisy and keeps important KPIs visible.
Sam (Product): Ooh. Curious about discoverability for keyboard users and screen readers though. Carousel + a11y is tricky. :thinking:
Adele (Frontend): I sketched an approach that preserves DOM order and uses aria-hidden + focus management. Quick snippet:
```js
// pseudo
container.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
 if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') focusNextVisibleTile()
})
```
Keeps tabs predictable.
Maya (Design): Nice. Also tried an alternate where the tiles compress to 2 columns with micro-wrapping — saves swipes but makes numbers tiny. Thoughts on legibility? :squint:
Zach (Eng): From infra side, repeated reflow is a perf risk if we measure complex rounding on every resize. Prefer simple media-query breakpoints and toggling classnames. Example CSS we discussed:
```css
@media (max-width: 520px) { .metric-grid { display: flex; overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; } }
```
Adele (Frontend): Agreed re perf. Also recommend a graceful fallback: if JS disabled, keep it stacked (no swipe), so content still accessible.
Sam (Product): Also copy nit — empty-state for metrics when user pins nothing: current copy is "No metrics yet". Suggest: "Pin important metrics to this dashboard — tap the pin icon on any card."
Maya (Design): Good call. On hit targets: mobile touch targets for the pin and overflow actions are currently 36px on the prototype — need 44px min. I updated Figma.
design-bot: Figma file updated: https://figma.com/file/abc123/metrics-mobile — Artboards: carousel-v1, compressed-grid.
Adele (Frontend): For keyboard/a11y we should expose previous/next buttons (visually hidden on touch but available to screen readers) and add role="region" aria-label on the carousel container.
Zach (Eng): Can we avoid infinite loop swiping? iOS rubber-band + sentinel tiles is annoying. Prefer simple linear scroll with visible gradient edges as affordance.
Maya (Design): I'll iterate on affordance and spacing. Action items: (1) Maya: update Figma with 44px touch targets and copy change. (2) Adele: prototype accessible focus trap and arrow key behaviour. (3) Zach: add perf notes about resize and overflow CSS. Sam: approve copy change?
Sam (Product): Approved the copy tweak. Small follow-up: can we run quick usability with 3 test users on staging? 5–10 min each.
Maya (Design): Yep I'll schedule a short session tomorrow. Thanks all :pray:
